decisions.statement: A 429 is a status a retry may be made against.
A 500 is a status a retry may be made against.
A 502 is a status a retry may be made against.
A 503 is a status a retry may be made against.
A 529 is a status a retry may be made against.
A status this module names nowhere is retried nowhere.
A response the server-error classifier does not match is retried nowhere.
A response the classifier does not match resolves with its own body.
Every retry goes to the account the failing attempt was made at.
Every retry has the token of the account being retried.
Every retry has the body of the request that failed.
A retry waits the schedule at the attempt's index.
A `retry-after` header sets the wait rather than the schedule.
A request makes one retry for each entry the schedule has.
An empty schedule makes no retry.
A retry that clears the error resolves with the retried response.
A retried status outside the retriable set resolves without being classified.
A retried status the classifier does not match resolves at once.
An error lasting through the schedule is answered persistent.
A persistent error has the body of the last attempt.
A persistent error has the status of the last attempt.
A persistent error is written about on the error seam.
Every retry is written about before that retry is made.
Every retry goes through `retry` so a dropped connection is tried again.
Each response body is read to text the once through `peek-response`.
The `retry-after` header is read off each attempt afresh.
A caller hands in the forward every retry is sent through.
A caller may hand in the schedule so a test needs no real wait.
A caller may hand in the sleep so a test needs no real wait.
Nothing here chooses an account.
Nothing here disables an account.
Nothing here reads a clock.
The schedule is read off `server-error` where the caller names no schedule.
The sleep is a real timer where the caller names no sleep.
Every line written here goes to the console rather than to a seam.
A body already sent upstream is sent again without asking whether sending that body again is safe.

definition: the attempts a request makes again at one account while upstream keeps failing
